Toyota Brings the Scion Back to the U.S., Now as the KEI-01 Mini Truck
35 photos
Photo: Toyota
For about 13 years or so in the 2000s and 2010s, American customers enjoyed the blessings, such as they were, of a wacky car brand called Scion. The over a decade of presence of the Toyota offshoot on the local market has not been easy on the company, though, and it went bust in 2016. Well, guess what?
Somewhat unexpectedly, Toyota announced this week the return of the Scion nameplate on American shores, but this time not as something that can be slapped on extremely small cars named iQ, xA, or tC. This time, it brings along an ultra-compact utility truck called the KEI-01.
The vehicle is, in essence, a local interpretation of the famous Japanese kei trucks. It plays in the low-speed vehicle class, meaning it can only travel at a maximum speed of 25 mph (40 kph), and it has some features here and there that are meant to honor the original Scion nameplate.
The mini truck is powered by a positively tiny 660cc three-cylinder engine, tied to a continuously variable transmission and a four-wheel drive system with auto mode and push-button lock.
At the back, the truck features a three-way fold-down cargo bed of undisclosed capabilities, while the front is occupied by an enclosed cabin with heat and air conditioning, large enough to accommodate reclining and sliding seats and interior cargo spaces.
When it comes to size, the KEI-01 is large enough to get the job done, while at the same time being small enough to become as nimble as possible: it stands 11 feet (3.35 meters) long and under five feet (1.5 meters) wide, and it is capable of carrying 600 pounds (272 kg) of cargo.
Toyota didn't go deeper into explaining everything the KEI-01 is capable of, saying it will do so closer to the launch date. Speaking of that, the truck will hit the market in the second half of next year, and it will be manufactured at Toyota’s Indiana Plant. Despite this, though, and the fact that it is meant for the American market, the vehicle will be offered in a right-hand-drive configuration.
Don't expect it to flood the roads in the hands of private owners, as this is an intentionally low-volume niche vehicle, and as such it will be offered at first to fleet customers. If all goes well, the KEI-01 will try to enter other segments as well later on.
Toyota sees the design as being ideal for use in a variety of activities, including urban commercial duties (especially delivery), farm work, campus jack-of-all-trades, and even for fun activities.
Toyota's mini truck is not the only vehicle to have been presented this week under the revived Scion brand. Two concepts have also been presented, the SxS and BKE. They are both meant to preview the potential development direction for the new Scion.
The SxS is really the same concept that was shown during the 2025 SEMA show. A side-by-side meant for off-roading by trade, it is powered by a turbocharged four-cylinder hybrid powertrain that delivers an incredible (for this kind of vehicle) 300 horsepower.
Toyota confirmed that the design will evolve even further, and it does have a solid chance of being produced sometime in the future.
The BKE, on the other hand, is a very strange contraption, a blend between an electric motorcycle and a stand-up scooter whose component parts and capabilities have not yet been disclosed at the time of writing.
